chains.title: T favors a GATA-family binding effect involving GATA3 at the TOX3-associated locus
chains.element: EH38E3180851, a distal enhancer-like cCRE containing the variant.

links.claim: GATA3 occupies the variant in MCF-7 and is highly expressed there. QBiC-SELEX predicts stronger T than C binding, but its best model is mapped from GATA2; this supports an alt-favored GATA-family sequence effect, not a GATA3-specific effect established by that assay.
The variant lies in the distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3180851. Its reported chromatin activity scores are maxima across biosamples, not MCF-7-specific measurements.

TOX3 is a plausible locus-level target because it is nearby and strongly prioritized by L2G, but the evidence does not connect EH38E3180851 directly to TOX3. The literature search found no variant- or element-specific functional validation, and no significant breast-tissue eQTL was reported.
GATA3 occupancy over the variant and high GATA3 expression are reported in the MCF-7 context; MCF-7-specific enhancer activity is not established by the supplied chromatin scores.

The T-favored sequence prediction is directionally compatible with the strongest reported T breast-cancer risk associations. TOX3 has gene-level breast-cancer support, but neither that support nor these data show that GATA3 mediates the association.

predictions: If this chain is correct, a variant-dependent enhancer readout should be more sensitive to GATA3 depletion than to FOXA1 depletion; the direction of the readout change is not specified.
A GATA3-focused allele-specific assay may show T-favored binding, though the QBiC-SELEX result alone does not establish this TF-specific effect.
falsified_if: A well-powered GATA3-specific allele-aware assay finds no T-favored binding in relevant breast cells.
GATA3 depletion leaves the variant-dependent enhancer readout unchanged while FOXA1 depletion selectively removes it.

matrix.test: Compare the effect of acute GATA3 versus FOXA1 depletion on a C/T variant-specific enhancer reporter in MCF-7 cells.

outcomes.outcome: GATA3 depletion selectively reduces the C/T reporter difference; FOXA1 depletion does not.
FOXA1 depletion selectively reduces the C/T reporter difference; GATA3 depletion does not.
Neither GATA3 nor FOXA1 depletion selectively removes the difference; NR2F2 dependence remains to be tested.
There is no reproducible C/T reporter difference to remove, or neither depletion changes it in a variant-dependent manner.

matrix.test: Measure allele-specific binding of GATA3, FOXA1, and NR2F2 at the locus in an informative heterozygous breast-cell sample.

outcomes.outcome: T-favored GATA3 binding is observed; this alone would not prove GATA3-specific causality.
T-favored FOXA1 binding is observed; this alone would not prove FOXA1-specific causality.
T-favored NR2F2 binding is observed; this alone would not prove NR2F2-specific causality.
No reproducible allele-specific binding difference is observed for the candidate factors.

matrix.test: Precisely edit C to T and measure enhancer activity and TOX3 expression in MCF-7 cells.

Editing changes enhancer activity and/or TOX3 expression, with a component dependent on FOXA1; the direction of expression change is not specified.
Editing changes enhancer activity and/or TOX3 expression, with a component dependent on NR2F2; the direction of expression change is not specified.
Editing produces no reproducible change in enhancer activity or TOX3 expression.

next_experiment: Use paired GATA3 and FOXA1 depletion with a C/T variant-specific enhancer reporter in MCF-7 cells, and test whether either depletion selectively removes the allele-dependent reporter difference. This is the cheapest proposed test that distinguishes the two leading chains.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr16:52565276:C>T, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap line ACH-000019), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 95 occupied (27 with a strong site), 5 of 75 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 45 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 411 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 22 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th. At a weak site the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element.
